case_name: Smt S R Ashwini vs G Harish

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Smt. S.R. Ashwini, W/O. G HARISH

facts_of_case: Petitioner filed RPFC No. 104 of 2018 against the order dated 20.07.2017 passed in C. MISC. NO. 128/2016 dismissing the petition filed under Sec. 125 of Cr. P. C. for maintenance.

legal_principles.principle: The object of maintenance proceedings is not to punish a person for his past neglect, but to prevent vagrancy and destitution of a deserted wife by providing her food, clothing and shelter by a speedy remedy.
legal_principles.held: This Court held that the object of maintenance proceedings is not to punish a person for his past neglect, but to prevent vagrancy and destitution of a deserted wife by providing her food, clothing and shelter by a speedy remedy.
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to understand the purpose of maintenance proceedings

legal_principles.principle: The husband is required to earn money even by physical labour, if he is able-bodied, and could not avoid his obligation, except on any legally permissible ground mentioned in the statute.
legal_principles.held: Since it is the sacrosanct duty of the husband to provide financial support to the wife and minor children, the husband was required to earn money even by physical labour, if he is able-bodied, and could not avoid his obligation, except on any legally permissible ground mentioned in the statute.
cited_cases: Bhuwan Mohan Singh v Meena and Ors (2015) 6 SCC 353
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to understand the husband's responsibilities

legal_principles.principle: A broad and expansive interpretation must be given to the term 'wife' to include even those cases where a man and woman have been living together as husband and wife for a reasonably long period of time.
legal_principles.held: A broad and expansive interpretation must be given to the term 'wife', to include even those cases where a man and woman have been living together as husband and wife for a reasonably long period of time.
cited_cases: Chanmuniya v. Virendra Kumar Singh Kushwaha and Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 141
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to understand the scope of the term 'wife'

legal_principles.principle: The law presumes in favour of marriage, and against concubinage, when a man and woman cohabit continuously for a number of years.
legal_principles.held: The law presumes in favour of marriage, and against concubinage, when a man and woman cohabit continuously for a number of years.
cited_cases: Chanmuniya v. Virendra Kumar Singh Kushwaha and Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 141
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to understand the presumption of marriage

outcome.final_order: The appeal is allowed and the order dated 20.07.2017 passed in C. MISC. NO. 128/2016 is set aside.
